open_obligations: Note the shift from 'too expensive to evaluate' to 'beyond human-level'.
Check which of Amodei et al.'s approaches (semi-supervised RL, distant supervision) Bowman et al.'s definition still covers.
Check that experiments citing either definition test the same problem.
in.rationale: Amodei et al. describe scalable oversight as the case where the correct objective is known or can be evaluated, e.g. by a human, but too expensively to do often. Bowman et al. define scalable oversight as providing reliable supervision (labels, rewards, critiques) that stays effective past human-level performance, citing Amodei et al.; the emphasis shifts from evaluation cost to capability beyond the supervisor.
in.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the definition of scalable oversight used to frame empirical oversight research

text: The authors describe the scalable oversight category as the case where the designer knows the correct objective function, or has a way to evaluate it such as consulting a human, but doing so frequently is too expensive, so harmful behavior can result from bad extrapolation from limited samples. Scalable oversight concerns how to ensure safe behavior given limited access to the true objective.
title: Scalable oversight: correct objective known but too expensive to evaluate often
